articles.title: Home Assistant recovers from a broken startup record
articles.dek: A Supervisor fix restores the recovery path when damaged container metadata leaves Home Assistant or an app unable to start.
body: An unclean shutdown can leave Home Assistant or one of its apps unable to start because the record describing its container is damaged. The Supervisor recognizes a specific form of this failure and removes the broken record so it can recreate the container, instead of failing on every startup attempt.

The problem followed a change in Docker, the software that runs those containers. It kept damaged records visible while rejecting normal operations on them, preventing the Supervisor from reaching its cleanup step. That could also block backups of an affected app or disrupt app authentication when Home Assistant Core was affected.

Stefan Agner's correction restores that recovery path and records which container had the problem. It addresses this particular metadata failure, not other forms of storage damage such as missing directories. Mike Degatano reviewed and approved the work.

pullRequests.title: Treat containers with corrupt storage metadata as missing

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps Sonos playing through short albums
articles.dek: A queue correction prevents speakers from falling silent, while a separate fix unblocks radio startup on older S1 models.
body: Sonos speakers can read several tracks ahead of what is playing. Music Assistant was refusing valid requests once a speaker got too far ahead of its own playback position, eventually bringing an album to a stop. The queue now measures those requests against the audio actually sent to the speaker.

Marcel van der Veldt tested the correction on a Sonos Beam with twenty 20-second tracks. Before the fix, playback stopped at track six; afterward, all twenty played without a refused request. Another correction prevents a failed preliminary check from marking an otherwise playable track as permanently unavailable in its queue.

Older Sonos S1 speakers had a different route to silence: starting radio could freeze Music Assistant while it waited for information from a speaker that was itself waiting for the stream. OzGav moves that query into the background so audio can keep flowing, with the original reporter verifying the fix.

articles.title: Z-Wave checks join Home Assistant's visual automation editor
articles.dek: Forms check device status, settings and values, extending this week's visual triggers to the conditions that follow them.
body: Home Assistant's automation editor gains forms for checking a Z-Wave device's status, configuration settings and reported values before an automation continues. The conditions can test whether any or all selected devices match, using named states instead of requiring their underlying numbers.

Raman Gupta's work follows the visual Z-Wave event and value-change triggers introduced earlier this week. Together, the changes bring both starting an automation and checking its prerequisites into the editor's forms. Existing per-device conditions remain supported.
The forms also catch mistakes before an automation runs: saving fails if none of the selected devices has the requested setting or value. An empty selection never counts as a successful match.

articles.title: Home Assistant gives wall panels a quieter kiosk display
articles.dek: The iOS app can hide its settings button and command confirmations while keeping a way back into settings.
body: Wall-mounted Home Assistant displays gain two ways to keep their dashboard uncluttered. The iOS app's kiosk settings can make the settings-entry button invisible and suppress the small confirmation messages shown after remote commands run.

Hiding the button does not lock people out: the same corner remains tappable. The app explains that behavior before saving the choice. The confirmation-message option applies on iOS 18 and later, and appears only while the kiosk accepts remote commands.
Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves's changes preserve the existing defaults. The settings button stays visible and command confirmations stay on unless the person configuring the panel chooses otherwise.

articles.title: Sendspin keeps untrusted audio out of spoken pairing
articles.dek: The protocol returns spoken setup codes to a speaker's own voice instead of accepting recordings from an unauthenticated server.
body: A speaker announcing a Sendspin pairing code should not have to play audio chosen by a stranger. The protocol removes a mechanism that let a server supply recordings of the ten digits before the two devices had established trust. Speaking clients instead use their own bundled voice, selecting its language using the server's language hint.

Chris's revision reverses an August specification decision that removed the need to store those voice clips on the speaker. Approved by maximmaxim345, the revised rule means an unauthenticated peer no longer gets to choose audio for the speaker or send audio into its decoder through this pairing mechanism.

articles.title: WindNerd brings a printed weather station to ESPHome's directory
articles.dek: A pre-flashed sensor board pairs with a 3D-printed wind instrument and an open configuration for home weather readings.
body: People building their own weather station have a new reference in ESPHome's device directory: WindNerd Node, a sensor board designed for an open-source, 3D-printed instrument that measures wind speed and direction.

The board comes with ESPHome pre-flashed, and its directory entry links to the maker's configuration for bringing readings into Home Assistant. Spare connections allow experiments with additional sensors, such as a rain gauge. The entry is khbenjamin's first contribution to the device directory, reviewed by Jesse Hills.

articles.title: Matter.js stops one command from crashing a controller
articles.dek: An unusual command limit could send the controller into an endless loop that exhausted its memory.
body: A single command to a Matter device could crash a controller built with Matter.js if the device reported that it accepted zero commands at a time. The protocol defines that value as meaning one, but the library treated it literally and kept creating empty batches until it ran out of memory.

Ingo Fischer's fix interprets zero correctly and checks other invalid limits before they reach command handling. It also corrects affected values when saved connection settings are read again, avoiding a separate storage migration.

pullRequests.title: fix(protocol): treat a peer's zero paths per invoke as one

articles.title: Home Assistant connects valve timers more directly to Apple Home
articles.dek: Valve run times can use an integration's own control, alongside new choices for how valves appear in HomeKit.
body: Home Assistant's HomeKit bridge can use a valve's integration-provided number control to set its run time, without requiring a separate number helper. A companion change lets native Home Assistant valves appear in HomeKit as faucets, shower heads, sprinklers or generic valves. Existing helper-based setups keep working.

The valve-type change is louwii17's first contribution to Home Assistant Core, with review and approval from Brett Adams and Markus Tuominen. Valves with no chosen type retain their generic appearance, and duration settings remain expressed in seconds.

articles.title: Qingping air-quality readings stop sticking at 290
articles.dek: The Bluetooth parser mistook a device-identification field for carbon dioxide, overwriting real measurements on the CGP22C.
body: A Qingping CGP22C could keep reporting carbon dioxide at 290 parts per million even as the air around it changed. A correction in the Qingping Bluetooth library stops a hardware-information field from overwriting the sensor's actual reading, following the manufacturer's confirmation of which field carries carbon dioxide.
Separate temperature-and-humidity updates also leave the last real carbon-dioxide reading intact. This is cp296944's first contribution to the repository, with review from bdraco.

pullRequests.title: fix: stop reading TLV 0x18 as CO2 on the CGP22C

articles.title: Home Assistant gives history timelines more room on phones
articles.dek: Names move below the bars, freeing the chart width without changing history cards on dashboards.
body: Reading a device's history on a phone gets less cramped. Home Assistant's History panel moves entity names from a left-hand column to below their timeline bars, giving the plot the full available width instead of squeezing it beside a truncated label.
Petar Petrov's change also reduces side padding on narrow screens and gives each timeline more vertical separation. Dashboard history cards and more-info dialogs keep their existing layout.

pullRequests.title: Move history timeline names under the bars

articles.title: Bluetooth history cleanup stops cutting off device connections
articles.dek: A library fix keeps nearby devices reachable while clearing old broadcasts—a failure observed with an ISEO Argo lock.
body: A nearby Bluetooth device could appear unreachable moments after its old broadcast data was cleared. In one reported case, an ISEO Argo lock failed to connect despite four Bluetooth proxies being a few metres away.

Federico Zivolo's first contribution to the habluetooth library separates the saved device record from the broadcast history being discarded. Connections can still use a scanner that saw the device, while the next broadcast is processed afresh. The fix was reviewed by bdraco.

pullRequests.title: fix!: keep the device record when clearing advertisement history

articles.title: Music Assistant fixes seeks that jump to the wrong moment
articles.dek: A correction for DSD music files restores playback timing and limits the memory used to hold decoded audio.
body: Some high-resolution DSD files gave Music Assistant a distorted picture of time: three seconds of decoded audio looked like twelve, and a request to jump to 1.5 seconds reached 0.375 seconds instead. The audio buffer counts the same sample format that the decoder produces, restoring the intended seek position.

The change also caps how much decoded DSD audio stays in memory, according to the chosen buffer setting. It is Michael Dobson's first contribution to the Music Assistant server, with review from Marcel van der Veldt and approval from Marvin Schenkel.

pullRequests.title: Fix DSD PCM buffer accounting and bound retention

articles.title: Assist learns mower commands in Italian and Malayalam
articles.dek: New phrases start mowing and send compatible robots home; Malayalam also expands vacuum controls.
body: Italian and Malayalam speakers gain ways to ask Assist to start a lawn mower or send it back to base. Italian support recognizes everyday names for a mower and natural requests to cut the grass. Malayalam adds mowing and docking commands alongside instructions for starting a vacuum, cleaning an area and returning to its base.

Francesco Sappa contributes the Italian phrases, approved by auanasgheps, while Arun S. Sekher adds Malayalam wording and replies. The new language patterns work with compatible devices already connected to Home Assistant.
